🛡️ Fraud & risk

Real signals computed from account data — shared devices, referral abuse, and unusual driver-rider pairing patterns

🆔 Identity collisions — one email or phone, more than one account

Ambiguous identity is what lets a ride event reach the wrong client

📱 Shared device / IP across rider accounts

Same device or IP behind multiple accounts — a classic promo/referral abuse pattern

🎁 Referral self-abuse

Referrer and referee sharing a device/IP — likely the same person claiming both bonuses

🤝 Unusual driver-rider pairing

Same pair riding together far more than random chance would suggest — worth a manual look, not proof of collusion

📍 GPS anomaly flags

Simulated — this dataset has no real live GPS stream to analyze for spoofing/teleportation patterns
A real deployment would flag: impossible speed between two pings, a trip's GPS staying fixed at one point the whole ride, or a route that doesn't match any real road path. None of these are computable from this dataset's static mock coordinates — flagging them here would be fabricating a signal, not detecting one.

How payouts work: quick-ride fares are payable as soon as a trip completes. Subscription payments are held in escrow and only released to the driver once the full plan is delivered (all required trips completed) — protecting against mid-plan cancellations or incomplete service.

Late pickups, no-shows
💵 How cash reconciliation works: when a rider pays a driver directly in cash (a trip fare, or extra cash to top up their wallet), the platform never actually receives that money. The system compares the GPS-and-pricing-based expected amount against what the driver reports collecting. A match (within a small tolerance) or a reported tip needs no action. An under-report (possible revenue leakage) or a driver who never reports at all gets queued below — the commission owed (and any wallet top-up the driver collected on the platform's behalf) is tracked as a running debt against that driver, deducted automatically from their next payout.

Matching & dispatch

🚕 Quick Rides

Live, second-by-second dispatch
Search phases — widen radius the longer a request waits
After (seconds)Radius multiplier

👥 Multi-subscription policy

When enabled — any driver can receive a new subscription regardless of how many they already have. When disabled — new subscriptions go only to drivers with zero active subscriptions ("new" drivers), unless a driver has a personal exception (set on their own profile).

📦 Subscriptions

Assigned once per cycle, not re-searched every second
No search-phase widening here — subscription trips are assigned once at creation/renewal, not re-offered second by second like Quick Rides, so a single fixed radius is enough. Applies to "Find replacement / Nearby drivers" tools too.

👁️ Plan visibility

Uses the Subscription radius above to check live coverage
Looking for pricing or commission instead? Subscription commission is set per plan on the Plans page — each cadence prices differently, so a single toggle here wouldn't fit.
🌍
Cities & regions
Add a city below, then flip it Active when ready. Active = riders in that city can search for and match with drivers instead of seeing "not available here". Driver applications are never blocked or told "we don't operate in your city yet" regardless of this toggle — approval works the same everywhere; the toggle only controls what riders can do. Districts and driver coverage within an active city are managed on the Zones & Coverage page.

🎨
Branding & logo
The mark shown at the top of the sidebar and on generated documents. Changing it affects every operator, so it sits behind a confirmation like any other shared setting.
💰
Pricing & rate card
Versioned, effective-dated, simulated before approval and never edited in place. Operations can suspend surge but cannot raise a price — the asymmetry is deliberate: an ops intervention is a safety action, and safety actions only ever reduce what a customer pays.
📒
Ledger & money safety
Double-entry postings and idempotency keys — the two things that stop money being paid twice or going unaccounted. Modelled here so the backend has an unambiguous specification: these accounts, these postings, these keys.
📟
On-call rota & shift handover
Who is actually reachable, hour by hour. A single standing assignment reads as coverage but escalates to somebody asleep — this names a person per shift and, more importantly, names the hours nobody covers.
🧮
Data integrity
Where a stored total disagrees with the records behind it. A summary kept next to the records it summarises will always drift; what matters is that the drift is visible instead of being resolved silently in favour of whichever surface rendered last.

🪟 Operational data window

🧮 Aggregate vs records

🏷️
Reason codes & SLA
The taxonomy every ticket, complaint, refund and contact is coded against — seeded from all 24 scenarios in the Call Center Communication Guide, plus 14 codes for events this panel already generates that the guide doesn't cover. SLA targets live on the code, not on the priority, because "High" tells an agent nothing about when: the guide's clocks (30-minute lost-item update, 24-hour misconduct follow-up, 48-hour complaint resolution) are properties of the scenario. Blank targets inherit the tier default below.

⏱ SLA tiers

Defaults inherited by any code that doesn't override them
TierFirst responseResolutionHoursPause when waiting on customer

🏷️ Reason code registry

—
CodeArabic labelCategoryTierFirst resp. (min)Resolve (min)Update everyRoot-cause ownerActive
Codes are never deleted or renamed — deactivate and add a successor, because historical records point at them. Every add, edit and deactivation is written to the activity log. If OTHER_UNCODED climbs above 3% of monthly contacts the taxonomy has gone stale and needs a review.

💰 Compensation authority

RoleMax per caseMax per dayIssued to date
A credit above 200 SAR needs a second approver, and any rider receiving more than 150 SAR or 3 credits in 30 days is flagged at the point of issue. Per-scenario ceilings live on the reason code above — a scenario set to 0 blocks goodwill entirely, because some problems are fixed rather than paid for.
